samf-senior-2016-r2-01.prompt: Joyce has a box with light bulbs, some blue and some red. She counts the bulbs and finds that 10 of the 40 are blue. What percentage of the bulbs are blue?

samf-senior-2016-r2-02.prompt: If $2016\times x$ is a perfect square, what is the smallest positive integer value for $x$?

samf-senior-2016-r2-03.prompt: For two positive real numbers $a$ and $b$, which may be equal, what is the smallest possible value of $\dfrac ab+\dfrac ba$?

samf-senior-2016-r2-04.prompt: In the four corners of the big square in the figure, squares with areas 9, 16, 25 and 49 are shaded. The two larger squares are touching. What is the area of the unshaded part of the big square?

samf-senior-2016-r2-05.prompt: The lengths of all sides of a triangle are prime numbers. If two sides are 5 and 7 what is the longest possible length of the third side?

samf-senior-2016-r2-06.prompt: Water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius and boils at 100 degrees Celsius. On the SAMO scale, water freezes at 20 degrees and boils at 170 degrees. The two scales are linearly related. What is the temperature on the SAMO scale if it is 80 degrees on the Celsius scale?

samf-senior-2016-r2-07.prompt: Each of the nine paths in a park is 100 m long. Ann wants to go from $X$ to $Y$ without going along any path more than once. What is the length, in metres, of the longest route she can choose?

samf-senior-2016-r2-08.prompt: How many two-digit positive integers $N$ have the property that the sum of $N$ and the number obtained by reversing the order of the digits of $N$, is a perfect square?

samf-senior-2016-r2-09.prompt: The faces of a cube are labelled with 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7, so that the numbers on opposite faces add up to 9, as shown in Figure 1. When four such cubes are placed as shown in Figure 2 the numbers on each pair of touching faces add up to 10. Which number is represented by the $*$?
samf-senior-2016-r2-09.reviewNote: Solution follows the official key; the arrangement of cubes in Figure 2 was not independently checked.

samf-senior-2016-r2-10.prompt: Let $P$ be the product of any three consecutive positive odd integers. What is the highest common factor (greatest common divisor) of all such numbers $P$?

samf-senior-2016-r2-11.prompt: If $AB$ is equal to the radius of the circle, what is the value of $\angle ACB$, in degrees?

samf-senior-2016-r2-12.prompt: If $f(x)=2^x$, what is the value of $\dfrac{f(x+1)+f(x)}{f(x)}$?

samf-senior-2016-r2-13.prompt: Simon and Harry spun a coin 30 times. Whenever the coin showed heads, Simon gave two sweets to Harry. When the coin showed tails, Harry gave three sweets to Simon. After 30 spins, both Simon and Harry had the same number of sweets as they started with. How many times did the coin show tails?

samf-senior-2016-r2-14.prompt: What is the minimum number of integers which must be removed from the first 50 positive even integers so that the sum of the remaining integers is 2016?

samf-senior-2016-r2-15.prompt: Triangle $BCD$ lies in the plane, and $A$ is a point outside the plane. $AB$ is perpendicular to the plane and $BD$ is perpendicular to $CD$. What is $\angle ADC$ in degrees? (The lengths marked in the figure are $AB=\sqrt3$, $BD=1$, $CD=\sqrt3$.)

samf-senior-2016-r2-16.prompt: $D$ is a point on side $AB$ of $\triangle ABC$, $E$ is a point on $CD$ and $F$ is a point on $CE$. The areas of triangles $AED$, $AEC$, $BFD$ and $BFC$ are 6, 10, 17 and 7, respectively. What is the area of $\triangle BEF$?

samf-senior-2016-r2-17.prompt: In $\triangle ABC$ the sides $a$ and $b$ are not equal, and $\angle ACB=90^\circ$. The numbers $x$ and $y$ are real, such that $\dfrac{x}{2a^2}+\dfrac{y}{c^2}=1$ and $\dfrac{x}{c^2}+\dfrac{y}{2b^2}=1$. What is the value of $x+y$ if $c=3$?

samf-senior-2016-r2-19.prompt: What is the remainder when $2^{2016}$ is divided by 13?

samf-senior-2016-r2-20.prompt: The diagram shown is formed by extending the sides of a right triangle and constructing four circles that are each tangent to all three sides. The radii of the three smaller circles with centres at $D$, $E$ and $F$ are respectively equal to 3, 4 and 21. What is the length of the radius of the circle with centre $G$?
